title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Malaysia
seo_title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Malaysia
meta_description: Malaysia's marathons and half marathons judged on official results: field sizes, finish times, women's share and fees, from Kuala Lumpur and Penang to Sabah's big halves.
dek: Malaysia is a half-marathon country. Almost every race in its calendar has a 21 km, and its fields are among the most relaxed in the region. These are the races worth choosing, and what the results say about each one.

sections.heading: What the data shows for Malaysia
paragraphs: Our calendar lists 100 Malaysian road races. 98 of them have a half marathon, but only 23 have a full marathon [1]. 86 of the 100 are dated between August and January. November is the busiest month, with August next, and February to July is thin [1]. Of the 44 races that publish fees, the median entry runs from RM45 for the shortest race to RM119 for the longest. The full range is RM20 to RM340 [1].

Our results cover seven Malaysian races and 23,882 finishers [2]. Across the seven half marathons (18,864 finishers) the median is 2:54, against 2:42 for the region as a whole. One finisher in ten takes longer than 3:44, and 7% break two hours. Women are 26% of half-marathon finishers [2]. The one marathon in the sample, the Malaysia Marathon in Kuala Lumpur, had 1,370 finishers, a median of 5:58 and 5.5% under four hours, the slowest big marathon field we track. Women were 14% of its finishers [2].

Read those numbers as good news for newer runners. A slow median means plenty of company at the back. The calendar can be unreliable, though: nine Malaysian races dated between 6 September and 25 October 2026 were cancelled, among them the Kuching Marathon and six JomRun-powered or mall-based half marathons [1]. Check a race's page close to race day. The full list is at runsea.run/regions/malaysia/.

sections.heading: Kuala Lumpur: the Standard Chartered marathon and the Malaysia Marathon
paragraphs: The Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon is the country's flagship. All of its categories start and finish at Dataran Merdeka, and it has 2 km and 800 m Kids Dash races alongside the marathon, half, 10K and 5K [3]. Entry was RM150 in our 2026 listing [1]. We don't hold its full results, so we can't compare its times, but it is the race most Malaysian runners measure the others against. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/kuala-lumpur-standard-chartered-marathon-klscm-2026/.

The Malaysia Marathon held its first edition on 30 August 2026, starting at Pavilion in Bukit Bintang and finishing at KLCC [1]. Its results suit a first marathon: a 5:58 median, finishers out to 7:32, and 15% of marathon finishers past 7 hours [2]. Its half drew 4,723 finishers with a 2:53 median, and its 10K had 3,648, 52% of them women [2].

sections.heading: Sabah: the biggest half in our Malaysian data
paragraphs: The Kota Kinabalu Half Marathon had 6,321 finishers in August 2026, more than any other Malaysian half we hold [2]. Its median of 3:02, with almost a quarter of finishers past 3:30, makes it the most forgiving big half in the country, and 31% of its finishers were women [2]. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/kota-kinabalu-half-marathon-2026/.

Sabah also has a marathon outside the state capital. The Elopura Marathon in Sandakan held its fourth edition on 22 November 2026, with full, half and 10 km races through the town and its surroundings [4].

sections.heading: Penang and the Klang Valley halves
paragraphs: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is run every year on the bridge that links Penang Island to the mainland [5]. Its marathon, half and 10 km are dated 13 December in our 2026 listing [1]. The other Penang race in the old guides is a different kind of event. The Travis Hegel Marathon du Trans Penang covers 41.76 km across the island, with 1,632 m of climbing, 40% of it on trail, and a 14-hour limit [6]. Treat it as a mountain day, not a marathon time.

Around Kuala Lumpur, the half-marathon fields are steady. The KL Half Marathon, powered by JomRun, starts at 3.30am at Padang Merbok [7]. It had 2,781 finishers with a median of 2:55 [2]. The Ultron half marathon from IOI City Mall in Putrajaya was the quickest Malaysian half in our data. It had 2,023 finishers with a 2:45 median, and 9% of them broke two hours [1][2].

sections.heading: Malls, stadiums and the JomRun circuit
paragraphs: Many Malaysian half marathons start from an unusual place. Our calendar lists 17 JomRun-powered races, and a large share of them start from a shopping mall. Shah Alam's starts at AEON Mall Shah Alam, Rawang's at AEON Mall Rawang, Kulai's at AEON Mall Kulaijaya, and the Johor Bahru City half at AEON Mall Bandar Dato Onn [1]. A mall gives a race car parks, toilets and covered space to wait in. On the other hand, four of the 2026 cancellations were mall-start halves in Nilai, Setiawangsa, Puchong and Johor Bahru [1].

Stadiums are the other common start. Kluang Stadium, Likas Stadium in Kota Kinabalu, the Sandakan Sports Complex and Miri's outdoor stadium all host races in our calendar [1]. A stadium start usually means a proper warm-up area and a controlled finish. The JomRun halves in our results are mid-sized and unhurried. The Johor Night Half Marathon had 1,408 finishers with a 2:46 median, and Terengganu had 1,171 with a 2:51 median [2].

sections.heading: Which to choose
paragraphs: For a first marathon, the Malaysia Marathon's results show the most room at the back. For a first half, Kota Kinabalu and the KL Half have big, relaxed fields. For a quicker half, the Ultron race in Putrajaya stands out. For the race most Malaysians want on their record, it's the Standard Chartered marathon at Dataran Merdeka. Whichever you pick, plan for the August-to-January season, when most of the calendar runs, and for a pre-dawn start: the KL Half sets off at 3.30am.

For how Malaysia compares with its neighbours, see runsea.run/articles/southeast-asia-biggest-flagship-marathons-ranked/. For a first race anywhere in the region, see runsea.run/articles/best-races-first-marathon-half-marathon-southeast-asia/.

faqs.question: What is the biggest half marathon in Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Of the Malaysian races in our results, the Kota Kinabalu Half Marathon had the most finishers in 2026: 6,321, with a median of 3:02. The Malaysia Marathon's half (4,723) and the KL Half Marathon (2,781) come next. We don't hold full results for the Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon.

faqs.question: How fast are Malaysian half marathons?
faqs.answer: Relaxed. The median across the seven Malaysian half marathons in our data is 2:54, against 2:42 for the region, and only 7% of finishers break two hours. The quickest field we hold was the Ultron half marathon in Putrajaya, with a 2:45 median.

faqs.question: How much does a race entry cost in Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Of the 44 Malaysian races in our calendar that publish fees, the median runs from about RM45 for the shortest race to RM119 for the longest. The full range is RM20 to RM340. Entry for the Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon was RM150 in our 2026 listing.

editorial_notes: Built from Run SEA's race calendar (100 Malaysian races) and results archive (7 Malaysian races with full results), with organisers' published race details checked on 6 Nov 2026. The Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon and the Penang Bridge race have no full results in our archive, so no times are given for them. World Athletics label tiers are not given. This is not a sponsored ranking.
